metadata.subject: DBMS
metadata.title: Commit or Roll Back
metadata.description: Operate on a working transaction and protect the committed database from partial changes.

learning_objectives: Distinguish committed data from a working transaction.
Predict COMMIT, ROLLBACK, and failure consequences.
Explain atomicity without assuming a full recovery engine.

mission.title: Run one complete transaction
mission.description: BEGIN, change the working copy, predict the durable result, then COMMIT.

introduction.title: A transaction protects a complete unit of work
introduction.content: Changes happen in a working copy first. COMMIT makes the whole unit durable; ROLLBACK or a pre-commit failure discards it.
points: Committed data is the durable starting point.
Working data can change without becoming durable.
A partial transaction must not be saved as if it were complete.

worked_example.title: Move a value as one unit
worked_example.content: A transfer contains two related changes.

steps.explanation: BEGIN creates a separate working state.
Both changes happen in the working state first.
COMMIT makes the complete working state durable.

worked_example.conclusion: If failure occurs before COMMIT, the committed state must not contain only half the transfer.

next.title: Now you try.
next.content: Watch committed and working data separately while you control the transaction.

action_explanations.begin: BEGIN copied the committed data into a working transaction.
action_explanations.apply: The operation changed only the working copy; committed data stayed unchanged.
action_explanations.commit: COMMIT made both related changes durable together.
action_explanations.failure: Failure before COMMIT discarded the working copy instead of saving a partial result.

problem.instruction: Transfer 20 units from A to B and commit both changes as one transaction.

challenge_problem.instruction: A failure occurs after removing 5 units from warehouse A but before adding them to B. Predict the durable inventory.

actions.label: Apply the debit to working data
Apply the credit to working data

challenge.title: Failure and atomicity challenge
challenge.start_message: Keep committed and uncommitted data separate.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. The durable state stayed consistent.

phases.title: Handle a pre-commit failure
phases.instruction: Run until failure and correctly predict the durable inventory.
phases.feedback: Failure before COMMIT must discard the working copy.

guidance.start_message: Complete both working changes before COMMIT.

items.content: Committed data changes only at COMMIT.

phases.title: Commit a complete transfer
phases.instruction: Run both operations and predict the committed result.
phases.feedback: Keep working and committed balances separate until COMMIT.

phases.title: Apply rollback
phases.instruction: Stop at the configured point and predict durable state after ROLLBACK.

guidance.start_message: Handle a failure at an unknown operation boundary.

phases.title: Solve a failure
phases.instruction: Follow the condition and predict the durable state after failure.
phases.feedback: A pre-commit failure cannot save a partial transaction.

guidance.start_message: Interpret the generated terminal condition independently.

phases.title: Master transaction outcomes
phases.instruction: Run the correct lifecycle and predict every durable field.
phases.feedback: Check the terminal condition and committed values.

thinking.title: Predict the durable database
thinking.instruction: Mentally follow the displayed operations and terminal condition. The final committed state stays hidden.
thinking.do_not_execute: Track working changes separately from committed values.

prediction_fields.label: Final status
prediction_fields.prompt: What status will the model end in?

prediction_fields.label: Committed A
prediction_fields.prompt: What durable value remains for A?

prediction_fields.label: Committed B
prediction_fields.prompt: What durable value remains for B?

feedback.all_correct: You separated working and durable state correctly.

quiz.question: A failure happens before COMMIT after only the debit. What should remain durable?

discovery.title: Transaction discovery
discovery.summary: A transaction isolates working changes and makes them durable only as a complete committed unit.

sections.title: Working state
sections.content: Operations first change an uncommitted working copy.

sections.title: COMMIT
sections.content: COMMIT makes the complete working state durable.

sections.title: ROLLBACK and failure
sections.content: Discarding the working state protects the committed database from partial work.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Atomicity means all of the unit becomes durable, or none of it does.

alternate_explanations.title: Edit a draft
alternate_explanations.content: Working data is like an unsaved draft; COMMIT saves it, while rollback closes it without saving.

alternate_explanations.title: Follow a transfer
alternate_explanations.content: Subtract 20 from A and add 20 to B in working state; only COMMIT changes both durable balances.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why must a failure before COMMIT not leave half a transaction durable?
recall.model_answer: The related changes form one atomic unit, so a partial working result must be discarded.
